query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 5 wt% chromium to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxidation resistance at high temperatures without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Oxidizing, Exposure time: 100 hours, Mechanical-loading boundaries: Strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective chromium oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The added chromium will react with oxygen to form a protective Cr2O3 layer, reducing the oxidation rate of the underlying alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in oxidation-induced mass gain relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, with no significant change in yield strength
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in oxidation resistance may vary depending on the specific chromium content and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation-induced mass gain of the chromium-modified alloy is not at least 20% lower than that of the untreated alloy after 100 hours at 1000 °C, the hypothesis is falsified
